judges: R.M. Sahai Mr. D.N. Diwedi J.
case_name: Smt. Sarla Mudgal, President, Kalyani & ... v. Union Of India & Ors
facts_of_case: The petitioners claimed that the government should endeavour to secure a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage solemnized according to one personal law cannot be dissolved according to another personal law simply because one of the parties has changed their religion.
legal_principles.held: I can find no authority for the view that a marriage solemnized according to one personal law can be dissolved according to another personal law simply because one of the two parties has changed his or her religion.
cited_cases: Robasa Khanum vs. Khodadad Bomanji Irani (1946 Bombay Law Reporter 864)

legal_principles.principle: A spouse cannot force their newly acquired personal law on the other party to a marriage by changing their religion.
legal_principles.held: Do then the authorities compel me to hold that one spouse can by changing his or her religious opinions (or purporting to do so) force his or her newly acquired personal law on a party to whom it is entirely alien and who does not want it?
cited_cases: Smt. Sarla Mudgal, President, Kalyani & ... vs Union Of India & Ors (1995)

outcome.final_order: The court held that the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code through-out the territory of India.

use_for_drafting: advising on bigamy and polygamy cases
